Classify

/KLAS-uh-fy/ · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Classify means to arrange things systematically into defined classes or groups based on shared qualities.

At the new branch, the librarian spent a week classifying donated books by subject before any could reach the shelves.

Worked Example

The biologist spent the whole morning working to classify the beetle specimens, placing each one in a group according to its wing structure and habitat.

She is assigning each beetle to a group based on shared physical traits — wing structure and habitat — which is exactly what it means to classify.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

categorize: Categorize means to place things into a set of defined categories — classify's closest everyday twin. Classify tilts more formal and technical: a biologist classifies specimens inside an official scheme, while a blogger might categorize posts by topic. When the system is scientific or official, classify is the stronger fit.

group: Group means simply to gather like items together — the loosest of these words, implying no system at all. Classify demands more: assigning each item to a defined class inside an organized scheme. Friends can group photos into rough piles; a curator classifies them by period and school.

catalog: Catalog means to record items one by one in an organized list, the way a library logs each new book. Classify is about grouping rather than listing: you classify items into classes, while cataloging captures each item's own entry. You can catalog a collection without grouping it at all.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

jumble: to mix into a disordered heap

scatter: to throw about randomly

Where it sits · how formal the grouping method is — sort → classify → systematize

sort vs. classify: Sort is looser than classify — you can sort laundry into lights and darks without any formal system behind the piles.

systematize vs. classify: Systematize goes further than classify — it builds an entire organized framework of rules, not just assigns items to their groups.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — class-

Root — class-: a group, rank, or division (Latin classis, originally a division of the Roman people)

Suffix — -ify

Suffix — -ify: to make or cause to become (Latin -ficare, from facere, to do or make)

Put it together

Put it together: Class- ('a group or rank') plus -ify ('to make') builds the meaning literally: to make things into classes — to put each item into its proper group.

Use the root in a new word: declassify

Use the root in a new word: declassify: The agency agreed to declassify the fifty-year-old reports, officially moving them out of the secret category.

Root Check

Word Choice

Neutral / academic

You classify things by a shared quality ('classify the essays by argument type') or classify one thing as a member of a group ('the film was classified as a documentary'). Related word to watch: classification — classify names the act of grouping, while classification names the result, the category or system produced. Don't swap one for the other on test day.
